regions.pileup_clean: No sign of pile-up. Rate {rate} ct/s, {photons} photons per {frame} ms frame.
regions.pileup_fractions: Observed-to-model ratios in 0.5–2 keV — singles {s} ± {se}, doubles {d} ± {de}. With no pile-up both are 1.
regions.pileup_inconclusive: There is an excess of doubles, but core and wings could not be separated to decide (the region is not a circle). Rate {rate} ct/s, {photons} photons per {frame} ms frame.
regions.pileup_parts: Splitting the region: core {core} ± {core_error}, wings {wings} ± {wings_error}. Pile-up grows with surface brightness, so it would concentrate in the core.
regions.pileup_pileup: PILE-UP: the excess of doubles is larger in the core than in the wings ({gradient}σ), which is how pile-up behaves. Extract from an annulus excluding the core and redo the reduction.
regions.pileup_unexplained: NOT pile-up. The excess of doubles is real but equal in the core and in the wings ({gradient}σ apart) — pile-up would concentrate in the core. On a very soft source this is expected: epatplot's model assumes a harder spectrum, and near the energy threshold charge splits between neighbouring pixels with no coincidence at all. You can go on with the circle.

step.acquisition.description: Find the observation in the public XMM-Newton archive (XSA) and fetch its ODF, or point at an ODF you already have.
step.calibration.description: Builds the calibration index valid for the observation date (cifbuild) and ingests the ODF (odfingest). No other SAS task runs without these two products.
step.export.description: Delivers the products in the form PULSARIS fits: a CSV event list and an instrument profile built from the real responses.
step.filtering.description: Measures the high-energy background, discards soft-proton flares and produces the clean event list.
step.processing.description: Runs the official SAS chains that turn raw data into calibrated event lists: epproc, emproc, rgsproc and the OM chains.
step.regions.description: Defines where source and background photons come from, and checks for pile-up, which distorts spectrum and light curve at once. Click the image to move the region; drag an edge to change a radius.
step.spectra.description: Extracts photon counts per channel with this observation's own response (RMF and ARF), including phase-resolved slices.
step.timing.description: Corrects arrival times to the Solar System barycentre and searches for periodicity — first by epoch folding, then refining with Z²ₙ on unbinned times.
timing.barycentering: Running barycen on events and GTIs…
timing.bins_hint: Phase bins: up to {bins} keep every profile point at 2σ ({count} photons, amplitude {fraction}%). Bins play no part in Z²ₙ or the H-test, which use no grid — they only draw the profile.
timing.found: Period found: {period} s — Z²₁ = {z}, {contrast}× the surrounding noise level. Already filled in above; use Search to refine the grid and Refine for the final value.
timing.harmonics_hint: Harmonics: the profile carries power above the noise up to m = {m} — use that. Each harmonic costs two degrees of freedom: adding empty ones dilutes the significance, stopping early throws away real modulation. (The H-test m above is the argmax of Z²ₘ−4m+4 and is meant for significance; on a strong signal it wanders with tail noise and makes poor advice.)
timing.harmonics_ok: Harmonics: m = {m} is as far as the profile carries real power.
timing.need_barycen: The refined search requires barycentred events.
timing.need_clean: Filter the events before the barycentric correction.
timing.need_lc: Extract a light curve before searching for the period.
timing.need_period: Determine the period before folding the profile.
timing.need_region: Barycentred events and a source region are required.
timing.no_candidate: No period carries power in the fundamental component. The source may not pulse in this band, or the modulation may be below what the light curve reaches — try a narrower band around the spectral peak.
timing.others: Other candidates, with the contrast that decided between them: {items}. Low contrast at a long period is red noise; high contrast at a short period is usually a harmonic.
timing.refine_result: P = {period} s · Z²_{harmonics} = {z} · H = {h} (m = {m}, p ≈ {probability}) · pulsed fraction = ({fraction} ± {fraction_error})%
timing.refining: Refining with Z²ₙ on unbinned arrival times…
timing.rms_result: RMS fraction = ({rms} ± {rms_error})% over {harmonics} harmonics — use this one, the profile is not sinusoidal.
timing.search_unconfirmed: The peak is NOT confirmed on unbinned arrival times (H test: p = {probability}). Likely an alias of the curve's grid: check whether the period is a multiple of the bin.
timing.search_unconfirmed_short: Peak not confirmed — likely a binning alias
timing.searching: Searching for the period by epoch folding…
